correctness.rationale: The normalized Fourier coefficients are exactly F_n(1-bR_n)/pi, with F_n=a(1-(-1)^n exp(-pi a))/(a²+n²)>0. For fixed parity, R_n increases in n. The critical nonstandard comparison R_1>R_0 follows from 2sinh(pi a)>pi a(1+a²); this inequality follows from sinh t>=t+t³/6. Consequently min R_n=R_0<0 and sup R_n=1/a+pi E/(1-E)>0, with no finite-index attainment of the supremum. These give the exact closed interval including both sharp failures; Fourier uniqueness establishes strict finite-site positivity even with a missing constant coefficient. The stand-alone numerical checker passed 120 independent integrals and concrete exterior negative circulant witnesses but was not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The signed affine modification is the natural first Matérn-3/2-type correction to an intrinsic geodesic Laplace covariance. The sharp bounds quantify precisely how much such smoothing is allowed despite the known full Matérn failure. The endpoints reveal distinct global-mean and high-even-harmonic obstructions, and the positive edge approaches the invalid Euclidean-inspired coefficient with an exponentially small gap. This complete continuous-parameter classification has a motivated covariance-design interpretation and is not a fixed-size numerical table.
